 Monaca Resident Charged with Money Laundering and Wire Fraud in Relation to International Ghost Student Scheme
 November 20, 2026 
 (File Photo of a Gavel)
 Noah Haswell, Beaver County Radio News
 (Pittsburgh, PA)  United States Attorney Troy Rivetti announced today that a resident of Monaca has been indicted by a federal grand jury in Pittsburgh on substantive charges of money laundering as well as conspiring to commit wire fraud.
 The seven-count Indictment named twenty-nine-year-old Emmanuel Hilton as the sole defendant.
 According to the Indictment, beginning in late 2021, the Department of Education began receiving reports from various universities and colleges of an excessive number of student enrollment requests at those institutions, which had noticed a variety of unusual patterns with the student registrations.
 The Department of Education conducted analysis of the Free Application for Federal
Student Aid (FAFSA) system and identified patterns that were associated with username creation, common passwords which were based on identical password hashes, and reuse of the same physical address for multiple students.
 It appeared that FAFSA accounts were being created using stolen personally identifiable information (PII) of actual U.S. citizens.
 The fraud actors would enroll in a university or community college using the names of actual U.S. citizens once a FAFSA account was created.
 However, the enrollments did not represent the actual students in class, either online or in person, and they were referred to as “ghost students.”
 The Department of Education would either award a grant or issue a loan in the name of the ghost student, and the funds would be sent to the school that was where the ghost student was enrolled.
 The receiving school would subtract from the funds the tuition and fees that were owed to the school and the loan money that was remaining would be refunded to the ghost student.
 This refund was typically remitted to the ghost student via an electronic funds transfer to a bank account that was provided by actors that facilitated these fraudulent schemes.
 The Indictment alleges that, between June of 2023 and February of 2026, Hilton acted as a money mule by opening multiple bank accounts for the purpose of receiving fraudulently obtained Federal Student Aid (FSA) refunds in the names of identity theft victims, and further alleges that Hilton, who shared in the proceeds of the fraud, received approximately $1,065,048.79 in FSA funds, and electronically transferred stolen funds to co-conspirators in Kenya.
 Hilton could face a maximum sentence of up to 20 years in jail, a fine of the greater of $250,000 or twice the gross pecuniary gain, or both, provided by the law as to the conspiracy to commit wire fraud charge.
 Hilton could also face a maximum sentence of up to 10 years in jail, a fine of the greater of $250,000 or twice the amount of criminally derived property involved in the transaction, or both, provided by the law as to each of the six money laundering charges.
